findings.title: New middleware and the moved log attributes have no test
findings.body: The attributes `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `uname` used to be added inside the instrumentation middleware. They are now added by `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`, and `LoggerMiddleware` logs them only through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)`. I found no test in `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware` that covers `instrumentContext` or `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware`, and none that checks `LoggerMiddleware` output. If `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware` is removed from the chain in `pluginsintegration.go`, or moved after `NewLoggerMiddleware`, "Plugin Request Completed" silently loses its plugin and datasource fields and no test fails. A small test could call each of the four endpoints and check the attributes through `FromContext`.

findings.title: Test function keeps the old middleware name
findings.body: The constructor is renamed to `newMetricsMiddleware`, but the test is still called `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`. Rename it to `TestMetricsMiddleware` so the name matches the type under test.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards the logs written through it
findings.body: `FromContext` returns a fresh `NewTestLogger()`, as `New` already does. Anything logged through `logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, which is what `LoggerMiddleware` now does, is therefore invisible to a test that holds the original `TestLogger`. Returning `f` would let tests assert on those calls. Nothing in this PR relies on it, so this is optional.

contracts.action: Plugin request attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) move from the metrics middleware into a new ContextualLoggerMiddleware that is registered after it
contracts.equivalent_path: Old `instrumentContext` call inside `instrumentPluginRequest` in metrics_middleware.go. It ran only after `pluginTarget` succeeded, and only for QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics.
contracts.before_after: Before, the context was enriched inside the metrics wrapper. Now `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` enriches the context for the same four endpoints with the same attribute set, and the stream methods pass straight through as before. It sits before `LoggerMiddleware` in the chain, so the logger middleware sees the attributes. The one difference is that it also runs when the plugin is not registered, because `pluginTarget` is no longer a gate.
contracts.visible_effect: Log lines from the plugin client and downstream code still carry the plugin and datasource attributes. Log fields come out in a different order.
contracts.failure_mode: `QueryData` in the new middleware dereferences `req.PluginContext` with no nil check. `LoggerMiddleware` has a nil guard but the metrics middleware has none, so a nil request panics in the old code too. No new failure mode.

contracts.action: LoggerMiddleware drops its own pluginId/endpoint/uname/traceID/dsName/dsUID params and calls `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info`
contracts.equivalent_path: Old `logRequest` built the params by hand. `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` runs every registered `ctxLogProviders` entry. These are the context-attributes provider in log.go and the traceID provider registered in `tracing.ProvideService`.
contracts.before_after: Before, the traceID was added through `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)`. The tracing provider uses the same call with the same argument, so the output is equivalent. This holds only when `tracing.ProvideService` has run, which it does at server startup. `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` type-asserts the result to `*log.ConcreteLogger`. `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` returns either `cl` or `cl.New(...)`, both `*ConcreteLogger`, so the assertion succeeds.
contracts.visible_effect: The "Plugin Request Completed" lines carry the same fields as before, now through the contextual logger.
contracts.failure_mode: If the assertion failed, the wrapper falls back to `d.New()` and silently loses the context fields. That cannot happen with the current infra logger.

summary:
I found no defects in this PR. I read all eight files and the unchanged code they call, and checked that the logging refactor behaves the same as before.

- **`traceID`:** it is still logged. `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` runs the providers registered at `pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:91`, and that one calls `TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)`, the same call the old code made.
- **Plugin and datasource attributes:** `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` sets them for the same four endpoints and sits before `LoggerMiddleware` in the chain.
- **New `Logger.FromContext`:** the only implementers of the interface are the wrapper and `TestLogger`, and both have the method. The wrapper's type assertion to `*log.ConcreteLogger` always succeeds with the current infra logger.

I left three non-blocking suggestions:
- Add tests for the new middleware and for the `LoggerMiddleware` output. Nothing fails if the middleware is dropped from the chain or moved after the logger.
- Rename `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`, which still has the old name.
- Optionally make `TestLogger.FromContext` return `f`, so logs written through it can be asserted on.
